minutes.headline: TCP design committee reviewed toilet counts, entrances, sidewalks and traffic study; set January 13 and 27 meetings.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the design team finish the discussion cut short on Monday: plumbing fixture counts, department and exterior entrance design, subdividing the property, sidewalk and paving limits of work, and the traffic and parking study. No formal votes were taken. The team said it has enough guidance to continue cost estimating, and two January meetings were scheduled.

budget_items.what_was_said: The architect said the key is the number of fixtures because each carries a cost.
A cheaper value-engineered alternative to wall panels was offered, with a manual of choices before town meeting.
A member asked about the cost difference; the architect will get the information.
A member asked about cost difference; the architect will provide information.
The DPW director suggested including paving of the loop legs in the project to avoid asking for money later.
A member worried an added connection could cost extra for handicap ramps.
The design team will send materials to the cost estimator, with a draft budget at a second January meeting.

decisions.decision: Meridian to add a sidewalk connection toward the high school to the plans.
Property subdivision to be raised with the Select Board's representative as a possible separate action item.
Design team will continue cost estimating on current guidance.
Next meetings set for January 13 at 5:30 and January 27.
Ed to ask the traffic consultant about opening the west gate.

what_happened.line: The Building Design Committee took no votes and told the design team to keep cost estimating on the guidance given so far.
Meetings were set for January 13 at 5:30 and January 27; a draft budget is due at the second one.
The team will send materials to the cost estimator, with a draft budget at the second January meeting.
Meridian is to add a sidewalk connection toward the high school to the plans; a member raised possible extra cost for handicap ramps.
Subdividing the property is to be raised with the Select Board's representative as a possible separate action item.

why_it_matters: The design choices made now, such as fixture counts, finishes, paving and sidewalks, feed the cost estimate and draft budget that will become the project's price when residents are asked to vote on it at town meeting.
Whether paving the loop legs is in the project or left out decides if that money is asked for now or in a later request.
